date.note: Publication date; the first evidence is dated 21 September 1955 by Berkeley Lab.

key_value_text.quote: On Sept. 21, a week after operating crews had revived the Bevatron, Segrè and Chamberlain got their first evidence of the antiproton based on momentum and velocity.
key_value_text.value: First evidence of the antiproton on 21 September 1955, from momentum and velocity

name: Observation of Antiprotons
notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from the Nobel citation and Berkeley Lab History ("the discovery of the antiproton"), so the type follows the title (A16).

summary.plain: Chamberlain, Segrè, Wiegand and Ypsilantis reported negatively charged particles with the mass of a proton, made when the Bevatron beam hit a target. This was the antiproton, the first antiparticle of a heavy particle to be found.
summary.technical: Momentum and velocity measurements of negative particles produced in Bevatron collisions identified the antiproton; Berkeley Lab dates the first evidence to 21 September 1955.

title: Observation of Antiprotons
why_it_matters: The 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Emilio Segrè and Owen Chamberlain "for their discovery of the antiproton".
